subject: Integration discovery recap & technical asks
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Mitchell <lauren.mitchell@clearpathhealth.com>, Tom Reyes <t.reyes@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Integration discovery recap & technical asks

Hi Lauren / Tom —

Thanks again for the 45-minute call earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned before the technical deep-dive:

Summary of pain & goals (from your side)
- Primary: reduce triage time in patient intake by surfacing intent & structured fields from free-text clinical notes (~30–40% manual review today)
- Accuracy target: entity/slot extraction F1 >= 0.88 on core fields (patient name, complaint, urgency, meds)
- Throughput: handle bursts up to ~120 reqs/sec with median latency < 120ms for 1–2 token replies in the path that drives UI UX
- Security/compliance: must route through ClearPath VPC; SOC 2 evidence and audit logs required for vendor onboarding

Product fit notes (Redwood capabilities relevant)
- SDK + streaming: we can stream structured outputs to your UI to render incremental fields as they arrive
- Function calling / structured outputs: recommend using our structured output schema to return slots and validation flags (we will share a draft schema)
- Embeddings / rerank: useful for matching prior notes and canonicalizing entity mentions; we discussed a hybrid approach (embedding lookup + rerank) for deduplication

Open technical asks (see attached XLSX with details)
1) Sample payloads: can you share 3 anonymized example notes (short/long/abbreviated) and the expected structured extraction for each?
2) VPC connectivity: networking team will need IP allowlist + handshake; please confirm whether we should prepare a VPN or VPC peering worksheet
3) Eval criteria: confirm the gold-label fields that matter for SLOs (we assumed 6 core fields)
4) Failure modes: how should we surface low-confidence cases back to ClearPath UI? (auto-escalate vs. flag)

Proposed next steps
- You: send anonymized sample notes and point of contact for networking (Lauren/Tom) by end of next week
- Us: internal technical sync (Redwood infra + SDK) and a proposed structured-output JSON schema before the follow-up call
- Schedule: suggest 60-minute technical workshop week of Jul 27 — give two preferred slots and we’ll lock it in

Attachments: integration_asks.xlsx (spreadsheet of payloads, sample sizes, eval buckets), redwood-infra-summary.pdf (short infra & security checklist)

If this looks right I’ll loop Marissa (solutions eng) to scope the SDK changes and prototype plan.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

From: Lauren Mitchell <lauren.mitchell@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <t.reyes@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Integration discovery recap & technical asks

Thanks, Sergio — this is a helpful summary and aligned to what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Samples: we can produce 5 de-identified notes (mix of SOAP, triage notes, and intake forms). I will place them in the Drive link you shared and flag which fields are gold-label. Expect by EOD Thu 23 Jul.
- Security: procurement will need SOC 2 Type II and an attestation on data residency. We need to understand whether Redwood Private or Dedicated is the recommended model for early pilot (we’re risk-averse).
- VPC: networking prefers a peering approach if you support AWS VPC peering; otherwise we’ll open a VPN. I’ll introduce our infra person (Tom) if you want to start a technical channel.
- Latency: the 120ms target is for the UI render path. We can tolerate slightly higher tail latency if streaming allows progressive field population.

We’re very interested in an early POC to validate accuracy and UX. Can you share a short list of the SDK changes you anticipate so we can scope internal engineering time?

Appreciate it —
Lauren
Product Lead, Integrations — ClearPath Health
lauren.mitchell@clearpathhealth.com

Hi all — looping in from solutions/engineering to translate the asks into an actionable SDK plan. Quick notes and a proposed priority matrix below: 

High-priority (week 1–2)
- Structured-output schema: we'll draft a JSON schema for the 6 core fields + confidence and suggested corrective actions (auto-correct / flag / human-review)
- Streaming API: add an incremental events stream that emits partial field fills and a final commit message; this will let the UI show progressive results without waiting for full model completion
- VPC handshake doc: I’ll drop a one-page peering checklist for your networking folks

Medium-priority (week 2–4)
- Embedding index + reranker prototype: pipeline to index recent notes and run a light rerank step to canonicalize entities
- Local eval harness: small test harness to run your 5 samples through candidate models and generate an accuracy summary report

Lower (future)
- On-prem Private deployment (if procurement requires): this will need a separate proposal and timeline

Questions for ClearPath (short answers appreciated)
1) Do you have an internal PII scrub process we should run before we ingest samples? (yes/no)
2) Which AWS region should we target for the VPC peering?
3) Who is the procurement lead for SOC 2 validation?

Next internal step for Redwood: Sergio and I will map the feature list to engineering estimates and come back with an initial scope + time-to-prototype. I’ll attach the draft schema and the peering checklist before the technical workshop.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Perfect — thanks Marissa and Sergio. Quick answers to your questions: 
1) Yes, we have a PII scrub that strips identifiers and replaces names with tokens — will run all samples through that first.
2) AWS us-east-1 is preferred.
3) Procurement lead is Nadine Cho (nadine.cho@clearpathhealth.com); I’ll loop her into the thread when we’re ready to surface SOC 2 artifacts.

We’re good to meet the week of Jul 27. Preferred slots: Tue 28 Jul 10:00–11:00 AM ET or Thu 30 Jul 2:00–3:00 PM ET. We would like the workshop to include a short walkthrough of the streaming SDK and the proposed structured-output schema.

I’ll upload the 5 de-identified notes to the Drive and post the link in this thread by Thu EOD.

Thanks — looking forward to the prototype plan.

Lauren
